These are not intended to be the everyday schedule, but flexibility is an important part of the position. What We’re Looking For Technical capability matters, but reliability and ownership matter just as much. The right person: Shows up on time and prepared Communicates clearly and professionally Takes ownership of assignments through completion Keeps customers and teammates informed without being chased for updates Identifies roadblocks early and asks for help when necessary Can organize multiple projects and priorities Pays attention to details Documents their work Enjoys troubleshooting difficult technical problems Is comfortable interacting directly with customers Maintains a friendly, professional demeanor, including when projects become stressful Is willing to perform both engineering and hands-on implementation work Is curious and willing to learn technologies outside their existing experience Technical Experience Strong candidates should have experience with several of the following: Enterprise Wi-Fi Ruckus Wireless or comparable enterprise WLAN platforms Ruckus ICX, Cisco, Aruba, Juniper, or comparable Ethernet switching VLANs and 802.1Q trunking Layer 2 switching and spanning tree IPv4 networking and subnetting Static and dynamic routing DHCP and DNS Firewalls, NAT, and VPNs PoE/PoE+/PoE++ Network troubleshooting using packet captures, CLI tools, and diagnostic utilities Wireless RF fundamentals including RSSI, SNR, channel utilization, interference, channel planning, and transmit power Network equipment staging, installation, testing, and commissioning Experience with CBRS/private LTE/5G, fixed wireless, microwave, fiber networks, RF design tools, or spectrum analysis is a plus but is not required. If you enjoy owning a technical problem and helping a customer get from “we have a problem” to “it’s working,” you may enjoy this role. Candidates must be comfortable: Installing and replacing network equipment Working in equipment rooms, telecom closets, offices, and customer facilities Using basic hand tools Moving and installing typical networking equipment Traveling periodically for customer projects Occasionally working from ladders or at modest heights when necessary VALL Technologies does not operate a bucket truck, and tower or significant work-at-height activities are generally performed by specialized contractors. What Success Looks Like A successful engineer at VALL Technologies becomes someone our customers and team can depend on. When assigned a project, you understand the objective, prepare for the work, execute it professionally, communicate what happened, identify anything still outstanding, and make sure the project continues moving forward. You don’t need to know everything on your first day. You do need to care about getting things right. About VALL Technologies VALL Technologies is a Colorado-based wireless and network engineering company serving enterprise, municipal, education, hospitality, telecommunications, and other customers. We work across traditional IT networking and advanced wireless infrastructure, giving our engineers exposure to projects and technologies that are difficult to experience in a narrowly specialized networking position. You will partner with Account Executives, Solutions Engineers, architects, specialists, Customer Experience teams, Business Entities, partners and global account stakeholders across multiple countries and time zones. Ability to travel within the Americas and participate in global customer or team meetings across time zones, based on business requirements. Technical expertise in Service Provider technologies and routing, including experience with large-scale IP/MPLS networks, segment routing, network automation or comparable architectures.
